Here is the itemized extraction of William Sanday and Arthur C. Headlam's explicit positions and claims across the seven substantive/extended B001 items from their commentary, A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Epistle to the Romans (1895).
B001-1: Romans 4:3 / Genesis 15:6
S02F-E001
Proposed Evidence ID: S02F-E001
B001 Passage ID: B001-1
Author's Claim: In Romans 4:3, the Greek term ἐλογίσθη employs a financial accounting metaphor meaning "was set down on the credit side."
Supporting Quotation: "metaphor from accounts, 'was set down,' here 'on the credit side.'"
Printed Page Number: Page 100
1
NotebookLM Citation:
1
Textual Evidence Invoked: LXX legal usage of λογίζομαι in Genesis 15:6, Leviticus 7:8, 17:4, and Malachi 3:16.
Claim Type: Exegetical
Qualifications / Conditions: None.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
S02F-E002
Proposed Evidence ID: S02F-E002
B001 Passage ID: B001-1
Author's Claim: Paul maintains a stricter adherence to the text of Genesis 15:6 than James by focusing exclusively on faith rather than appealing to later narrative events like the offering of Isaac.
Supporting Quotation: "We notice at once that St. Paul keeps more strictly to his text. Gen. xv. 6 speaks only of faith."
Printed Page Number: Page 102
2
NotebookLM Citation:
2
Textual Evidence Invoked: Text of Genesis 15:6 in comparison with Genesis 22 (the offering of Isaac) cited in James 2:21.
Claim Type: Exegetical
Qualifications / Conditions: The authors note that Paul also appeals to particular historical incidents (such as belief in the birth of Isaac in Rom 4:18–21), but does so via a more searching exegesis grounded in Genesis.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
B001-2: Romans 9:25 / Hosea 2:23 [LXX 2:25]
S02F-E003
Proposed Evidence ID: S02F-E003
B001 Passage ID: B001-2
Author's Claim: Paul utilized an Old Greek manuscript tradition of Hosea 2:23 reflecting the reading of Codex Vaticanus (ἀγαπήσω τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην) rather than the majority Septuagint reading (ἐλεήσω τὴν οὐκ ἠλεημένην).
Supporting Quotation: "In the second clause St. Paul seems to have used a text containing the reading of the Vatican MS."
Printed Page Number: Page 264
3
NotebookLM Citation:
3
Textual Evidence Invoked: Presence of ἀγαπήσω in Codex Vaticanus (B) versus ἐλεήσω in the majority of LXX manuscripts and 1 Peter 2:10.
Claim Type: Textual-critical
Qualifications / Conditions: The authors observe that Codex Vaticanus can hardly have been altered retrospectively to harmonize with Paul.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
S02F-E004
Proposed Evidence ID: S02F-E004
B001 Passage ID: B001-2
Author's Claim: Paul inverted the clause order of Hosea 2:23 and substituted καλέσω for ἐρῶ under the verbal influence of ἐκάλεσεν in Romans 9:24 to emphasize the divine calling of the Gentiles.
Supporting Quotation: "St. Paul inverts the order of the clauses ... and for ἐρῶ substitutes καλέσω which naturally crept in from the ἐκάλεσεν of the previous verse"
Printed Page Number: Page 264
3
NotebookLM Citation:
3
Textual Evidence Invoked: Inversion of parallel clauses and substitution of καλέσω in Romans 9:25 compared with LXX Hosea 2:23.
Claim Type: Literary
Qualifications / Conditions: None.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
B001-3: Romans 9:26 / Hosea 1:10 [LXX 2:1]
S02F-E005
Proposed Evidence ID: S02F-E005
B001 Passage ID: B001-3
Author's Claim: The primary textual divergence between Paul's quotation of Hosea 1:10 in Romans 9:26 and the Septuagint is Paul's insertion of ἐκεῖ to stress the locus of divine reception.
Supporting Quotation: "The only difference between St. Paul's quotation and the LXX is that he inserts ἐκεῖ"
Printed Page Number: Page 264
3
NotebookLM Citation:
3
Textual Evidence Invoked: Insertion of ἐκεῖ in Romans 9:26 (ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος) against the uncial LXX text of Hosea 1:10.
Claim Type: Textual-critical
Qualifications / Conditions: The authors note that it is somewhat difficult to determine whether "the place" refers narrowly to Palestine/Jerusalem in Jewish eschatology or universally to any location on earth where Gentiles reside.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
B001-4: Romans 10:11 / Isaiah 28:16
S02F-E006
Proposed Evidence ID: S02F-E006
B001 Passage ID: B001-4
Author's Claim: Paul adds the universal quantifier πᾶς ("everyone") to his quotation of Isaiah 28:16 in Romans 10:11 to prove that faith in Christ is the universal condition of salvation for Jews and Gentiles alike.
Supporting Quotation: "Quoted from Is. xxviii. 16 (see above, ix. 33) with the addition of πᾶς to bring out the point on which emphasis is to be laid."
Printed Page Number: Page 290
4
NotebookLM Citation:
4
Textual Evidence Invoked: Prefixing of πᾶς in Romans 10:11 (Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων...) relative to Romans 9:33 (ὁ πιστεύων...) and LXX Isaiah 28:16.
Claim Type: Exegetical
Qualifications / Conditions: None.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
B001-5: Romans 10:13 / Joel 2:32 [LXX 3:5]
S02F-E007
Proposed Evidence ID: S02F-E007
B001 Passage ID: B001-5
Author's Claim: Paul quotes Joel 2:32 verbatim in Romans 10:13 to clinch his argument, applying the divine Old Testament name Κύριος directly to Jesus Christ.
Supporting Quotation: "the quotation agrees with both the LXX and the Hebrew texts ... The term Κύριος is applied to Christ by St. Paul in this connection."
Printed Page Number: Page 291
5
NotebookLM Citation:
5
Textual Evidence Invoked: Verbatim agreement between Romans 10:13, LXX Joel 3:5, and MT Joel 2:32; christological context of Κύριος in Romans 10:9, 12.
Claim Type: Exegetical
Qualifications / Conditions: The original Old Testament context refers to Jehovah in the eschatological "day of the Lord," which Paul interprets as the spiritual fulfillment of Messianic salvation.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
B001-6: Romans 11:34 / Isaiah 40:13
S02F-E008
Proposed Evidence ID: S02F-E008
B001 Passage ID: B001-6
Author's Claim: Paul cites Isaiah 40:13 in Romans 11:34 with only slight variation from the Septuagint to confirm the unsearchable depth of God's wisdom and judgments.
Supporting Quotation: "This is taken from Is. xl. 13, varying only very slightly from the LXX."
Printed Page Number: Page 340
6
NotebookLM Citation:
6
Textual Evidence Invoked: Agreement between Romans 11:34 (τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν Κυρίου; ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο;) and LXX Isaiah 40:13 (compared with 1 Cor 2:16).
Claim Type: Literary
Qualifications / Conditions: None.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
B001-7: Romans 15:12 / Isaiah 11:10
S02F-E009
Proposed Evidence ID: S02F-E009
B001 Passage ID: B001-7
Author's Claim: Paul's citation of Isaiah 11:10 in Romans 15:12 adopts the Septuagint's paraphrastic rendering to describe the Messianic reign of the "root of Jesse" over the Gentiles.
Supporting Quotation: "The quotation follows the LXX, which is only a paraphrase of the Hebrew"
Printed Page Number: Page 399
7
NotebookLM Citation:
7
Textual Evidence Invoked: LXX Isaiah 11:10 (ὁ ἀνιστάμενος ἄρχειν ἐθνῶν, ἐπʼ αὐτῷ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν) vs MT Isaiah 11:10 ("which standeth for an ensign of the peoples, unto him shall the Gentiles seek").
Claim Type: Textual-critical
Qualifications / Conditions: None.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
